name: Atlassian
exchange: Nasdaq (Class A Common Stock, Nasdaq Global Select Market)

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Atlassian-horizontal-blue-rgb.svg, the en.wikipedia.org Atlassian infobox logo)

description: Atlassian sells team-collaboration software: Jira (planning and tracking work), Confluence (shared knowledge), Jira Service Management (IT and customer support desks), Loom, Bitbucket, Trello and the Rovo AI assistant, bundled into 'Collections' on one cloud platform. Customers (more than 350,000, over 85% of the Fortune 500) mostly find and buy it on the website with little sales effort and then expand; 95% of revenue is subscriptions and the rest is mainly Marketplace commissions. Cloud is 67% of revenue and the older self-hosted Data Center products 28%, but Data Center is being wound down (no new customers since March 2026, support ends March 2029), so growth depends on moving customers to Cloud. Revenue grew 26% to $6.57 billion in the year to June 2026, but profit is thin: operating income was $10 million and net loss $54 million after $285 million of restructuring charges.

hq.note: Principal executive offices 350 Bush Street, San Francisco (FY2026 10-K cover). Founded in Sydney, Australia; Wikipedia's infobox still lists Sydney as headquarters, see conflicts.

employees.note: Full-time employees (FY2026 10-K Item 1). Over 50% work in R&D. A restructuring in fiscal 2026 affected about 10% of the workforce.

businessLines.name: Cloud
businessLines.how: Per-seat monthly or annual subscription that grows as a customer adds users, moves up to premium and enterprise editions or Collections, and uses AI credits (Rovo); price increases also contributed to FY2026 subscription growth.
businessLines.description: Subscriptions to Atlassian-hosted apps (Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Loom, Rovo, Bitbucket and others) and the Collections that bundle them, on the Atlassian Cloud Platform.

businessLines.name: Data Center
businessLines.how: Annual term-license subscriptions to run the software on the customer's own servers; the product is being end-of-lifed in phases so these customers are pushed to Cloud.
businessLines.description: Self-hosted versions of Atlassian apps that customers run on their own infrastructure, sold as on-premises term licenses plus maintenance.

businessLines.name: Marketplace and other
businessLines.how: Atlassian sells third-party add-on apps through its Marketplace and handles license management and renewals for the vendors (the 10-K does not state the commission rate).
businessLines.description: Atlassian Marketplace, where third-party vendors sell add-on apps for Atlassian products (more than 6,000 apps and integrations), plus other minor revenue.

brands.name: Jira / Jira Service Management / Confluence / Loom / Rovo / Bitbucket / Trello / Compass / Jira Product Discovery / Focus / Talent / Guard
brands.segment: Apps sold stand-alone or inside Collections
brands.note: Revenue by app is not reported; the 10-K gives revenue only by deployment option.

brands.name: Collections (Teamwork, Service, Strategy, Software, Product)
brands.segment: Bundles of apps plus Rovo credits
brands.note: Revenue by Collection is not reported.

brands.name: The Browser Company of New York (Dia and Arc browsers)
brands.note: Acquired 2025-10-20 for $488.3M ($481.5M cash plus $6.8M non-cash); revenue not separately reported.

brands.name: DX (A Software Company)
brands.note: Acquired in fiscal Q2 2026; revenue and price not read.

whatsNext.text: Data Center wind-down: sales of term licenses and expansions to existing customers stop in March 2028; maintenance and support for Data Center products planned to end in March 2029
